plan.purpose: Confirm the largest post-collection retention PSS difference with balanced label order and a same-baseline-library control. Both allocators exhibited both footprint modes in the original three pairs; the second process in each pair had the larger footprint.

acceptance.response: Retain and investigate findings with longer paired holdouts; do not widen limits or omit cases. Memory and HTTP p99 remain separate metrics.

plan.order: Alternate old/new order by paired round, reverse case order every other round. Compare the same cached executable and fixed allocator alias/input paths for both labels. All builds and copies complete before timing.
plan.runtime_inputs: active-allocator.so and active-worker paths are identical for both labels. Move each completed worker directory to its recorded archive path between serialized jobs. Label and actual library SHA are recorded outside worker configuration.
plan.statistics: Median paired candidate/baseline normalized-time ratio per case. HTTP uses baseline/candidate throughput. Equal-weight geometric mean per suite/profile; report each component, memory metrics, p99 and quality flags separately. No cross-suite overall score.
limits: Normal interpose feature mode; full secure application coverage is not claimed.
Nginx uses the documented default five-second load with three paired repetitions; over-limit results require longer confirmation.
Local closed-loop HTTP load may be generator or upstream limited; preserve all quality flags.
Retention is an observation with an A/A calibration; idle duration is not allocator work and no mixed timing/memory score is computed.
plan.analysis: Report absolute and baseline-adjusted settled PSS in bytes and paired candidate-minus-baseline differences, alongside both footprint modes. Two A/A rounds calibrate the same workload.
